stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Complex multi-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature requires full elaboration (openspec) followed by testability/security hardening (speckit). No dependencies blocking spec work. Priority high due to empty AC preventing implementation.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live-preview mechanism exists. useContent (236 callers) is the single content-fetching chokepoint and the required attachment point. ACs were empty; VCs derived from description. Contentstack API is unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of the boundary (what request we make, how we handle responses).

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with useful context: useContent (236 callers) is the content-fetching chokepoint, Contentstack API is unreachable at test time, and this is a novel capability. All 14 ACs are new additions derived from the story description, title, and file paths. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-7/AC-8 establish the activation boundary — preview mode is opt-in via valid token/params and inactive otherwise. (2) AC-2 sets a 5-second freshness target for real-time updates; this threshold is a placeholder and should be validated by the team. (3) AC-3/AC-4/AC-5 cover the three brands explicitly per the story title. (4) AC-6 and AC-9 address error/fallback paths — critical since the Contentstack API is unreliable at test time. (5) AC-8 is a security gate preventing unauthorized draft access. (6) AC-10 ensures the request boundary is correct without naming implementation. (7) AC-11/AC-12 cover accessibility — preview indicator and loading-state announcements. (8) AC-13 covers session termination. (9) AC-14 covers referenced/linked content, inferred from ContentstackLink.tsx in the file list. CAVEAT: File contents were unavailable; criteria are derived from description, title, and paths alone. If useContent.ts or contentstack.ts contain existing preview-related logic, some ACs may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified the architectural chokepoint (useContent, 236 callers) and the test-boundary constraint (Contentstack API unreachable at test time), while speckit translated that context into 14 concrete, testable ACs covering activation, freshness, multi-brand, error/fallback, security, accessibility, session lifecycle, and linked content. However, openspec's contribution was context-only — it produced zero ACs despite being the elaboration agent, which is below expected output quality. Speckit compensated but the pipeline imbalance is a concern. The 14 ACs appear complete and non-overlapping, but several issues require human review: (1) The 5-second freshness target (AC-2) is explicitly a placeholder needing team validation. (2) File contents were unavailable — all ACs were derived from description, title, and file paths alone; if useContent.ts or contentstack.ts contain existing preview logic, ACs may need adjustment. (3) No story split was produced (splitCount: 0) despite this being a complex multi-market (GO, UP, MX) feature touching 236 callers — a split into activation, rendering, error-handling, and accessibility stories may be warranted. (4) acceptanceChanged is false for both agents despite 14 new ACs being added, which suggests a metadata tracking issue.
